featureGrid.title: AI agents that work on their own, but never merge on their own

items.title: Spec-driven
items.description: The Planner writes a spec with numbered acceptance criteria first. A blocking question stops the run and is asked on the ticket, and an approved spec is never edited by an agent.

items.title: Plan → Implement → Verify
items.description: Every task runs through Plan → Implement → Verify. A failing gate retries once, then stops with a Draft PR and hands off to a human.

items.title: Every phase leaves a file in your repo
items.description: Each phase's output is stored as a Markdown file in the repo — not chat context that disappears once the session ends.

items.title: Starts when a ticket is ready
items.description: The Orchestrator is triggered automatically when a ticket becomes ready — a Linear workflow state or a GitHub Issue label. Jira support is planned.

items.title: Checkers never edit what they check
items.description: The Validator checks every acceptance criterion and the Reviewer checks the diff against the spec. They write a report and don't change the code they are checking — a failure goes back to the implementation agent.

items.title: Human decides the merge
items.description: The agent chain runs by itself up to an open pull request, and can wait for you to approve the spec first. Merging is always an explicit human decision — there is no auto-merge.

pipeline.title: The agent chain runs itself — merging never does
pipeline.description: Once a ticket is ready, the agent chain runs on its own up to an open pull request. It pauses for a person only on an open question, an optional spec approval, or a gate that keeps failing — and {review} is always a human decision.
pipeline.ariaLabel: CAF Orchestrator pipeline diagram: a ticket becomes Ready for AI in Linear or GitHub Issues, then flows through the Planner, an optional spec approval, the implementation agents, the Validator, the Reviewer and an optional Docs agent, opens a pull request, and waits for a human to merge it. An open question, a spec approval or a gate that keeps failing pauses the run for a person, and there is no auto-merge.

ticket.title: Ticket
ticket.subtitle: Linear · GitHub Issues
ticket.detail: Triggered when a ticket moves into Linear's "Ready for AI" workflow state, or a GitHub Issue gets the ready-for-ai label. The same trigger resumes a run that paused for an answer: move the ticket back to Ready for AI, or re-apply the label. Jira support is planned but not yet implemented.

plan.title: Plan
plan.subtitle: Planner writes the spec
plan.detail: The Planner agent reads the ticket and writes requirements.md with numbered acceptance criteria, plus tasks.md — the spec the rest of the chain works from. An open blocking question stops the run: the draft spec is pushed to the branch, the question is asked on the ticket, and the Planner continues from your answer when the ticket is triggered again.

approve.title: Spec gate
approve.subtitle: Optional human approval
approve.detail: A ticket with the spec-approval label stops at a Draft PR that holds only the spec. A human reviews it and comments /caf-approve-spec to continue. Tickets without the label skip this step.

implement.title: Implement
implement.subtitle: Frontend/backend
implement.detail: Frontend and backend agents write the code from their own section of tasks.md and write verify-report.md with one line of evidence per acceptance criterion. If that report is not SUCCESS, the run stops with a Draft PR.

validate.title: Validate
validate.subtitle: Reports, never fixes
validate.detail: The Validator agent checks every acceptance criterion by running its evidence itself. It writes validate-report.md with PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED per criterion and does not change code. On FAIL the implementation agents retry once; if it still fails, or every criterion is UNVERIFIED, the run stops with a Draft PR.

reviewer.title: Reviewer
reviewer.subtitle: Verdict
reviewer.detail: The Reviewer agent reviews the diff against the spec and writes review-notes.md with a verdict: APPROVE, CHANGES_REQUESTED or DEFER. CHANGES_REQUESTED sends the work back to implementation once; if it is still requested, the run stops with a Draft PR.

docs.title: Docs
docs.subtitle: Optional docs agent
docs.detail: If the plan includes docs tasks and the repo has a documentation agent, it updates the docs affected by the change. Otherwise this step is skipped. A docs error never fails the run.

pr.title: PR
pr.subtitle: Branch pushed
pr.detail: The branch is pushed and a pull request is opened automatically, with an acceptance-criteria summary and the artifact chain in its description, and the link is posted on the ticket. A resumed run updates the existing Draft PR and marks it Ready for review.

merge.title: Merge
merge.subtitle: No auto-merge
merge.detail: The one step that is always a human decision. When a gate keeps failing, the run stops with a Draft PR holding the failing report — fix it by hand, or comment /caf-retry-pipeline to resume. Nothing ever merges automatically.

pipeline.onFail: If it fails: Draft PR for a human

items.question: What is CAF?
items.answer: CAF (Coderium Agent Framework) is an AI agent orchestration framework that takes a ticket from a written spec to a pull request through Plan → Implement → Verify, with strict governance — automated quality gates along the way, and a human decision before anything is merged.

items.question: What does spec-driven mean in CAF?
items.answer: The unit of work is a written spec, not a chat message. The Planner writes it, a human can approve it, and implementation, validation and review are all checked against its acceptance criteria. Agents never edit an approved spec; they propose changes and a human decides. The code stays the source of truth — it is not generated from the spec.

items.question: Is CAF free?
items.answer: Yes. CAF is free and open — you run it directly in your own repo and infrastructure, with no license fee.

items.question: Which trackers are supported?
items.answer: Linear and GitHub Issues are supported through CAF Orchestrator today. Jira support is planned but not yet implemented.

items.question: Which AI runner does it use?
items.answer: Claude Code. CAF Orchestrator runs each agent — Planner, implementation, Validator, Reviewer, and Documentation when the repo has it — as a headless Claude Code process. The same agents also run directly in a Claude Code session.

items.question: Can CAF auto-merge?
items.answer: No. CAF Orchestrator opens the pull request automatically once the quality gates pass, but it has no merge step. Merging is always a human decision.

items.question: Does CAF store my code on a third-party server?
items.answer: No. CAF Orchestrator runs on your own VPS, and the artifact handoff between phases is just a Markdown file in your repo — your code is never sent to a Coderium server.

about.title: About
about.metaDescription: CAF is built by Coderium — why, and for what problem.
about.heading: Built by Coderium
about.p1: CAF (Coderium Agent Framework) is built and maintained by Coderium, a studio building developer tooling with a focus on agentic coding you can actually trust — not just fast.
about.p2: Many of today's agent coding tools have a narrow scope (helping with just one small part of the development cycle) or loose governance (auto-merging with no guarantee of human review). CAF was built to fill that gap: a wide implementation scope — from ticket to PR — paired with strict governance: quality gates between the stages and a human decision at the end.
about.p3: We believe AI agents can speed up development without sacrificing control. That's why every change passes automated gates — verify, validate, review — before a PR is opened, why a failing gate stops and hands off to a human instead of pushing on, why nothing is ever merged automatically, and why CAF Orchestrator deliberately runs on your own infrastructure, not as a service managed by Coderium.
about.p4: CAF is a separate project from Coderium's main site. To learn more about Coderium as a studio, visit Coderium's main site (coming soon).

changelog.heading: Release history
changelog.intro: CAF Initiator is at v0.1.11, and CAF Orchestrator is at v0.2.0 — this page will keep growing with future releases.

items: caf-design and caf-breakdown are written without the DRAFT banner (their dispatch tests passed), so a new Planner is pointed at both
caf-architect is no longer offered in the agent picker: the Planner writes design.md. A caf-architect.md already in a repo is left alone

Terminal UI, pnpm tui (pnpm start:tui after a build): starts and stops the web server, worker and Cloudflare tunnel; shows queue and Redis / DB / HTTP health, summary cards, the run list, a text Agent Floor, live logs, a command palette (ctrl+p) and a failed-job list with retry. No browser, login or running web server needed
Cloudflare tunnel runner, pnpm tunnel, so Linear and GitHub webhooks reach a local machine. TUNNEL_NAME, TUNNEL_URL, TUNNEL_TARGET_URL and CLOUDFLARED_BIN in .env; also controlled from the TUI

Dashboard login page at /dashboard/login with a signed, HttpOnly session cookie (12 hours) and a Log out button, replacing browser Basic Auth. Same dashboard.basicAuthUser and DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD credentials

DASHBOARD_DEFAULT_VIEW (dashboard or agent-floor) chooses what /dashboard shows. The Agent Floor moved from /dashboard/agent-floor to /dashboard/floor/*, and its header shows total and average cost per run

Validation gate chosen from the checkout: caf-validator (validate-report.md) when .claude/agents/caf-validator.md exists, otherwise caf-qa. The docs step is skipped, not failed, when there is no caf-documentation agent (SDD-04a)

Acceptance-criteria summary at the top of the PR body, and the rule that a PASS report whose criteria are all UNVERIFIED becomes NEEDS_HUMAN. The gate is stored as validate; a stored qa is still read (SDD-04b, 04d)
Clarify via the ticket: a NEEDS_CLARIFICATION spec, or a DRAFT with an unanswered BLOCKING question, stops the run and asks in a ❓ CAF-CLARIFY comment (SDD-04c, 04d)
Spec gate: tickets with the spec-approval label stop at a Draft PR that holds the spec until /caf-approve-spec; a resumed run that succeeds marks the PR Ready for review (SDD-04c, 04d)
readFixReviewLog ends comment blocks on a ## line only after the Status line and outside a code fence (SDD-04e)

Restricted validator: caf-validator runs under dontAsk with an allowlist of Bash commands, writes limited to .caf/tasks/ and a stripped environment; agents.validator.restrictBash and allowedCommands (SDD-04f)
Git authentication without a token in the workspace: each network command uses a per-process extraheader. Needs git 2.31 or newer (SDD-04g)
caf-design skill and design.md: the Planner writes a technical design when a ticket spans apps, changes a schema or changes a contract (SDD-05a)
caf-breakdown skill and breakdown.md: the Planner proposes how to split a request with several outcomes and stops; /caf-plan may create the tickets one at a time after a yes (SDD-05b)
Planner artifact contract names design.md and breakdown.md in one place; an outline spec has no acceptance criteria and says Tidak ada (SDD-06)
Clearer agent text: ## Coverage in tasks.md, the reviewer's verdict for a finding only a human can settle, the validator's checklist scope and pipes in report tables (SDD-07)
caf-spec v4, aligned with the Planner: Tidak ada for an empty section, Assumption A-n:, and a fourth Status value NEEDS_HUMAN (SDD-10)
The Planner writes its artifacts in the language of the ticket author, not of text the ticket quotes (SDD-11, SDD-12)
CAF.md aligned with the spec-driven behavior (SDD-09)
Spec-driven Planner: Specify → Clarify → Plan → Tasks, requirements.md with numbered acceptance criteria and a Status line; caf-spec and caf-traceability skills (SDD-01, SDD-02)
Spec-aware implementation agents, Reviewer and review commands: read the spec first, stop on an unclear spec, report evidence per criterion, never edit an approved spec (SDD-03b, 03d)
New caf-validator agent and /caf-plan are part of the default scaffold, in place of caf-qa; the validator runs Verify: command: lines under strict rules (SDD-03b1, 03c2, 03e)

Five agents and eight commands are no longer scaffolded: Documentation, DevOps, PM, UX Designer, Auditor and the discovery, audit, design-ticket, qa-check, review-ticket and feature-catalog commands. Existing files stay (SDD-03c1)
SINGLE_REPO now gets caf-frontend and caf-backend instead of caf-implementer (SDD-03c3)
/caf-run-pipeline is now /caf-run, and /caf-plan-ticket is no longer written (SDD-03c2c)
Skill caf-verify renamed caf-self-verify, with a skill-renamed warning in curate audit (SDD-03c2d)
curate skips agent files of an unknown kind and reports them instead of rewriting them (SDD-03g)

curate reads the app list back from the Input of QA and Reviewer agents, so a sync no longer drops it; rollout warnings for frontmatter tools, skill pointers and the Planner's Constraints (SDD-03a2, 02d)
CAF skills (CAF-SKILLS-01): caf-init scaffold skills writes five universal skills into .claude/skills/ — caf-verify, caf-scope-discipline, caf-no-guess, caf-escalate, caf-piv
Agent definitions get an optional ## Skills section with Read pointers to the skills; agents generated after the skills exist get their pointers automatically
Existing agents are offered the ## Skills section with a preview and per-file confirmation — written only when the result is the old file plus exactly that one section
caf-verify is built from the scripts detected in package.json; a missing script leaves a TODO line and a DRAFT banner, and agents ignore a DRAFT skill
curate --check-drafts now covers skills: missing skill files, pointers to DRAFT skills, open TODOs without a banner, and a half-removed DRAFT banner
/caf-complete-drafts handles DRAFT skills and never invents a verification command
README rewritten
SINGLE_REPO support: a repo without workspaces is now a first-class mode, not an error — the repo root is the only app
New --mode flag (single or mono) on scaffold, docs and curate to override repo-mode detection
Single-repo implementation agent caf-implementer, with --scope to limit it to directories and --role frontend or --role backend to generate it as caf-frontend.md / caf-backend.md for CAF Orchestrator
AI-assisted draft completion: scaffold complete-drafts generates the /caf-complete-drafts command — it fills TODOs from the code and asks first for human-owned content
curate --check-drafts: a read-only check of completed drafts (changed tracked sections, non-existent scripts, leftover placeholders, missing golden-example paths)
A leftover generate-time template placeholder now aborts the write
MONOREPO output is frozen by a snapshot test
Role-aware Report Format and Retry Logic for the qa and reviewer kinds
caf-qa.md gets its own Report Format: qa-report.md with a Status line of PASS or FAIL, matching what CAF Orchestrator parses
QA and Reviewer Retry Logic now name their own report file instead of verify-report.md
Kind-aware Report Format for caf-reviewer (CAF-REVIEWER-FORMAT-01)
caf-reviewer.md gets its own Report Format section — fixed Verdict skeleton (APPROVE / CHANGES REQUESTED / DEFER) written to .caf/tasks/review-notes.md
Previously only the auditor kind had a Report Format; reviewer branch added to buildReportFormatSection(kind)
buildAuditContractSections(kind): reviewer gets Report Format only (no What to Look For — scoped to the Verdict contract, not review criteria)

Skeleton copied verbatim from caf-orchestrator's buildInitialReviewPrompt() to stay word-for-word compatible with report-reader.ts's strict/loose Verdict parsers (no shared import between packages — drift risk noted in code)
Regression tests added: test/reviewer-report-format.test.js
README updated
Content-level section tracking system (CAF-CURATE-DIFF-01)
curate command: content-level section tracking (baseline/current/template 3-way diff → IN_SYNC/DRIFT/CUSTOMIZATION/CONFLICT/UNTRACKED)
curate baseline command — backfills the manifest for untracked sections, never edits content
Section parsing is now fence-aware (handles ``` blocks, avoids false section boundaries)
Retry logic added for discovery agents and section guards
devops added to KNOWN_KINDS (fixes misclassification as implementation, a privilege-escalation risk)
Discovery section builders (Tools/Input/Output) got real pm/ux-designer branches — no more generic-fallback DRIFT false positives
Idempotency check aligned with the webhook's initial review posting method
Test script added to package.json plus a large test suite expansion (agents sync, manifest gen, devops handling, retry logic, Discovery sections)
Docs updated: section tracking and retry logic explained
Initial CAF release: PIV discipline (Plan → Implement → Verify), one retry before handing off to a human
CAF Initiator — CLI scaffold generator with automatic stack detection
CAF Orchestrator — self-hosted webhook receiver (Fastify + BullMQ + Redis)
5-layer architecture: Project Knowledge Base, Agent Definitions, Artifact Handoff, Quality Gates, Orchestration
Tracker integration: Linear (Jira planned)
Git host integration: GitHub (GitLab planned)
Mandatory human-review checkpoint at every phase — no auto-merge

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.metaDescription: Terms of use for CAF (Coderium Agent Framework).
terms.heading: Terms of Service
terms.s1Body: CAF (Coderium Agent Framework) is a framework — a set of code, conventions, and tooling you run yourself in your own repo and infrastructure. CAF is not a SaaS service hosted by Coderium. No instance of CAF Orchestrator is run or managed by Coderium on your behalf.
terms.s2Body: CAF's code — CAF Initiator and CAF Orchestrator — is distributed under the MIT license. See the LICENSE file in each repository.
terms.s3Body: CAF is free and provided as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. There's no SLA (service level agreement) on the free version — no commitment to response time or uptime, since CAF Orchestrator runs on your own infrastructure, not Coderium's.
terms.s4Body1: Agents run by CAF may produce code that is incorrect, incomplete, or doesn't match intent. This is consistent with CAF's own governance principle: mandatory human review before any code is merged. You — not Coderium — are fully responsible for the decision to review, approve, or merge any change an agent produces.
terms.s4Body2: Coderium is not liable for any loss arising from the use of CAF, including but not limited to code defects that pass human review.
terms.s5Body: These terms may change as CAF evolves. Changes will be announced in the project's changelog.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.metaDescription: What data the CAF site stores, and how your code stays private.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.s1Body: This is the most important point: CAF Orchestrator runs on your own VPS, not on a Coderium server. The artifact handoff between phases (see Layer 3: Artifact Handoff) is just a Markdown file stored in your repo. Your project's source code is never sent to, or stored on, Coderium infrastructure.
privacy.s2Body1: This marketing and documentation site (the one you're reading now) currently doesn't run any third-party analytics. If we add analytics in the future, we'll prioritize privacy-friendly tools (like Plausible or Umami) that don't do cross-site tracking, and this page will be updated to say so explicitly.
privacy.s2Body2: We don't collect email addresses or other personal data through this site — there's no newsletter form or account signup.
privacy.s3Body: Variables like tracker API keys or Git host tokens (see Environment Variables) are stored in an .env file on your own infrastructure. Coderium never receives or stores these credentials.
privacy.s4Body: If you have questions about this privacy policy, reach us via GitHub.
